column1: # TITLE: miRNA expression profiling in malignant transformation of human bronchial epithelial cells induced by arsenite

# SUMMARY: miRNA Array was used to detect the expression level of miRNAs in human bronchial epithelial (HBE) cells that were transformed by a low-level arsenite exposure for 13 weeks. The transformed cells exhibited malignant phenotypes manifested by increased levels of cell proliferation
column2: cell migration and high level of cell survival. Subsequently
column3: 191 differentially expressed miRNAs are identified to be associated with arsenite-induced malignant transformation by employing miRNA Array. Among them
column4: six miRNAs were chosen to validate their expression levels with qPCR and 17 miRNAs were further explored their target genes and the network. Three databases
column7: were used to predict the target genes of miRNAs and a total of 954 common genes were identified. Results of Gene Ontology (GO) analyses showed that these target genes were involved in diverse terms of GO categories
column8: such as positive regulation of macroautophagy
column9: epithelial cell maturation and synaptic vesicle clustering and so on. Moreover
column10: results of KEGG pathway analyses demonstrated that most of these target genes were enriched in various cancer-related pathways including non-small cell lung cancer
column13: p53 signaling pathway and so forth. The miRNA-gene regulatory network
column14: which was constructed by cytoscape software with miRNAs and their target genes
column15: showed that the target genes were mainly regulated by miR-15b-5p
column16: miR-106b-5p and miR-320d. Although more experimental verification is still needed to prove these predictions
column17: our results may provide new insights into miRNA-mediated mechanisms underlying arsenite-induced malignant transformation.
